not: used to make a statement, verb, or phrase negative
The results are not as clear as we had hoped.
only: and no one or nothing more besides; just
Only a handful of tickets remained by the time we arrived.
also: The recipe also works well with chicken instead of beef.
landslides: sudden falls of earth or rock down a slope
Heavy rain triggered several landslides along the mountain road.
landers: spacecraft designed to land on a planet or moon
Several landers have explored the surface of Mars since 1976.
seismic: relating to earthquakes or ground vibrations
Engineers designed the bridge to withstand strong seismic activity.
faults: The mechanic checked the car for any hidden faults.
hints: slight signs or suggestions of something
những gợi ý, dấu hiệu nhỏ
The report contains hints of a possible policy change.
lava: hot melted rock that flows from a volcano
Glowing lava slowly flowed down the side of the volcano.
tubes: plural of tube; long hollow cylinders
Scientists have found landslides, landers, seismic faults, and even lava tubes on the Moon.
regularly: often, at even and predictable intervals
She visits her grandmother regularly, usually every Sunday afternoon.
analyze: to examine something in detail to understand it
Scientists use special software to analyze samples collected from distant planets.
close-up: a photograph or view taken at very close range, showing fine detail
The magazine printed a close-up of the rare orchid in bloom.
portions: amounts of food served or eaten at one time
The restaurant is known for serving generous portions at reasonable prices.
taken: removed, carried, or done (past participle of take)
đã được lấy, đã thực hiện
The photo was taken during their trip to the coast last year.
narrow-angle: having a small field of view, as with a zoomed-in camera lens
The narrow-angle lens captured fine detail on the distant cliff face.
look: to direct one's eyes in order to see
Look both ways carefully before crossing the busy street.
typically: in a way that is usual or characteristic; usually
The assembly itself typically accounts for only a thin slice of the final value.
every: used to refer to each member of a group without exception
Somebody must repaint the roof every few years.
few: a small number of; not many
Only a few students finished the exam before the bell rang.
searches: She searches online for cheap flights every few weeks.
wider: measuring a larger distance from side to side
The gap between city and countryside grows wider still with added warmth.
features: distinctive or notable parts or qualities
The new laptop has several useful features, including a longer battery.
creating: causing something new to exist; bringing into being
The company is creating dozens of new jobs in the region this year.
global: relating to the whole world; worldwide
Climate change is a global problem requiring international cooperation.
older: having lived or existed for a longer time; comparative of old
Older buildings in the city often lack modern insulation.
versions: particular forms of something that differ from others
Different versions of the story exist across the region.
doing: What are you doing this weekend?
oct: abbreviation for the month of October
The conference was originally planned for Oct. 15.
when: The baker's skill lies in knowing when to wait and when to stop waiting.
came: moved toward or arrived at a place or state; past tense of come
Help finally came after they had waited for nearly three hours.
wide-angle: describing a camera lens that captures a broad view
He used images from a wide-angle camera to capture a broad view of the surface.
which: used to ask about or refer to a specific choice
It is one of the clearest ways in which a city changes its weather.
captures: obtains or secures a share of something; records accurately
The company captures most of the profit from the new invention.
broad: wide in extent, or general rather than detailed
The teacher gave a broad overview of the whole course.
views: opinions, or scenes that can be seen from a place
He shared his views on the new policy at the meeting.
pixels: the smallest single units of a digital image
The old photo looked grainy because it had so few pixels.
hundreds: several hundred of something; a very large number
Hundreds of people lined up outside the new store.
frames: rigid structures that support something, or individual images in a sequence
The animator drew hundreds of frames for a few seconds of film.
software: the programs and instructions used to operate computers
The company develops software for managing hospital records.
designed: planned and created for a purpose
The bridge was designed to withstand strong earthquakes.
highlight: The report highlights several weaknesses in the current system.
change: A single ingredient can change the whole flavour of a dish.
anything: If you need anything during the trip, just call me.
stayed: continued to be in a place or condition
đã ở lại, tiếp tục tồn tại
Prices stayed roughly the same throughout the summer.
turned: past tense of turn; changed direction or became something different
Both guesses turned out to be backwards.
gray: of a colour between black and white; American spelling of grey
The sky turned gray just before the storm hit.
while: It makes the city liveable while the wider problem is dealt with separately.
different: not the same as another or each other
Every student in the class has a different learning style.
showed: past tense of show: proved or made clear that something was true
The photos showed clear signs of damage after the storm.
patches: small areas or parts that differ from their surroundings
The old jacket had faded patches on both sleeves.
process: a series of actions taken to achieve a result
Learning a new language is a slow and gradual process.
sounds: gives a particular impression when heard or considered
Your plan sounds reasonable, so let's try it.
straightforward: easy to understand or do; uncomplicated
Filling in the online form is fairly straightforward.
spotting: noticing or detecting something, often something unusual
Spotting the error early saved the company a lot of money.
real: actually existing; genuine, not imagined or fake
The documentary tells the real story behind the famous painting.
requires: needs something, or demands it officially
This recipe requires fresh herbs and a hot oven.
lot: They spent a lot of money renovating the old house.
manual: done by hand rather than by machine
The old factory still relies heavily on manual labour.
work: activity involving effort, especially to earn a living or achieve something
The difference is not impatience on one side; it is what is doing the work.
flags: The spell-checker flags any word it does not recognize.
tiny: very small in size or amount
A motorbike can reach a front door in these alleys and park in a tiny space.
shift: to move or change gradually from one state to another
Public opinion began to shift after the documentary aired.
lighting: the equipment or quality of light in a place
ánh sáng, hệ thống chiếu sáng
The restaurant's dim lighting created a cosy atmosphere.
shadow: a dark shape cast when something blocks light; something that closely follows
Private tutoring has grown into a huge shadow industry in many countries.
generating: producing or bringing something into existence
The new policy is generating a lot of public debate.
false: The witness gave a false statement to the police.
alarms: devices or signals that warn of danger
Smoke alarms should be tested at least once a month.
reason: a cause or explanation for something
Nobody knew the real reason for his sudden resignation.
verifies: checks that something is true or correct
The system automatically verifies each user's identity before granting access.
fuzzy: not clear or sharply defined; blurred
The old photograph looked fuzzy after being enlarged.
halos: circles of light surrounding bright points
Photographers noticed faint halos around the streetlights in the fog.
pixelwide: as wide as a single pixel
A pixelwide line appeared across the sensor image after calibration.
points: indicates or suggests something as likely or true
The evidence points to a sudden change in weather patterns.
indicate: point out or show something clearly
A red light on the panel will indicate a system fault.
splashes: marks or patterns caused by liquid or material scattering onto a surface
Rain left small splashes of mud across the freshly painted wall.
spanning: extending across or covering an area or period of time
The exhibition features photographs spanning fifty years of history.
stood: was in an upright position; remained in a certain place or state
The old clock tower stood untouched for over a hundred years.
immediately: Please call the doctor immediately if symptoms worsen.
obvious: easy to see or understand; clear
It was obvious from her face that something was wrong.
pattern: a regular, repeated way in which something happens or is arranged
Analysts noticed a clear pattern in the company's sales figures.
i've: I've never seen such a beautiful sunset before.
seen: The old photographs had not been seen for decades.
takes: gets hold of, requires, or needs an amount of time or effort
The journey usually takes about two hours by train.
sharper: having a finer edge or clearer definition
The new camera lens produces a much sharper image.
per: The hotel charges eighty dollars per night for a standard room.
pixel: the smallest single unit of a digital image
Zooming in revealed that each pixel was slightly blurred.
flew: travelled through the air, especially by aircraft
The plane flew over the mountains just after sunrise.
again: She read the letter again before deciding what to write back.
revealed: The investigation revealed serious flaws in the safety system.
shape: the outward form or outline of something
The cookie cutter gave the biscuits a star shape.
surrounding: Smoke from the fire drifted over the surrounding countryside for days.
terrain: an area of land, especially with regard to its physical features
The hikers struggled across the rocky, uneven terrain.
affected: Families affected by the flood received emergency housing support.
helped: gave assistance to; past tense of help
Volunteers helped clear debris after the storm passed.
force: physical strength or power exerted on something
The wind hit the coast with tremendous force.
rock: the hard solid material forming part of the earth's surface
Water had worn a deep channel through the soft rock.
fragment: a small piece broken off from something larger
Archaeologists found a fragment of ancient pottery near the site.
details: Please fill in your contact details at the bottom of the form.
expected: Removing any single support does less damage than expected.
appear: to become visible or to seem to be the case
Stars begin to appear in the sky shortly after sunset.
future: the period of time that is to come
Nobody can predict exactly what the future holds.
